ques: Browse the Well-Being section filtered to the Sleep topic, open the article about how to fall asleep faster, and report the name of the doctor who medically reviewed it.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open the article detail page /articles/fall-asleep-faster. (2) The answer MUST name the medical reviewer Miguel Santana (Miguel Santana, MD) from that article's byline. (3) Empty answer is a FAIL. FAIL if the article page was never opened or a different reviewer is reported.

ques: In the Health News section, filter to the Research & Approvals topic, open the article about RSV vaccines for adults in their 50s, and report both its published date and its medically reviewed date.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open /articles/rsv-vaccine-adults-50s (the RSV-vaccine-for-adults-in-their-50s article, NOT the RSV-in-infants article). (2) The answer MUST report BOTH the published date (December 23, 2024) AND the medically-reviewed date (December 27, 2024). (3) Empty answer or only one date is a FAIL.

ques: In the Diet & Weight Management section, filter to the Food & Recipes topic, open the article listed there, and report who wrote it and which doctor medically reviewed it.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open /articles/meal-prep-90-minute-system (the Diet & Weight > Food & Recipes article). (2) The answer MUST name BOTH the author Sofia Andersson AND the reviewer Danielle Hart (Danielle Hart, MD). (3) Empty answer or only one name is a FAIL.

ques: Use the site search to find the article about how much water you actually need, open it, and report who wrote it, which doctor medically reviewed it, and which topic it is filed under within its section.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open /articles/hydration-how-much-water. (2) The answer MUST report the author Sofia Andersson, the reviewer Karen Shale (Karen Shale, MD), AND the topic/subcategory it is filed under: Healthy Living. (3) Missing any of the three, or an empty answer, is a FAIL.

ques: Search the site for the brand name Flomax, open the matching drug's page, and report the standard adult starting dose and exactly when the page says it should be taken relative to meals.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open the Tamsulosin drug page /drug/tamsulosin (reached by searching Flomax). (2) The answer MUST give the standard adult starting dose 0.4 mg once daily AND the timing: about 30 minutes after the same meal each day. (3) Empty answer, wrong dose, or missing timing is a FAIL.

ques: Search for melatonin and open the article about what the evidence supports. Report the name of its medical reviewer, then open that reviewer's author profile and report the credentials listed there.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open /articles/melatonin-evidence AND the reviewer profile /authors/steven-marsh-pharmd. (2) The answer MUST name the reviewer Steven Marsh AND report the credentials on his profile: PharmD, BCPS. (3) Empty answer or missing credentials is a FAIL.

ques: Open the drug page for warfarin and report the three antibiotics that its interactions section specifically names as raising bleeding risk.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open the warfarin drug page /drug/warfarin. (2) The answer MUST name all THREE antibiotics its interactions section calls out: ciprofloxacin, azithromycin, and amoxicillin. (3) Fewer than three, wrong drugs, or an empty answer is a FAIL.

ques: Open the levothyroxine drug page and report the category label shown at the top of the page and the conditions listed in its 'Used For' sidebar.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open the levothyroxine drug page /drug/levothyroxine. (2) The answer MUST give the category label (Hormones & Thyroid) AND the conditions in the 'Used For' sidebar: Hyperthyroidism (Overactive Thyroid) and Hypothyroidism (Underactive Thyroid). (3) Missing the category or either condition, or an empty answer, is a FAIL.

ques: From the Migraine condition page, open the triptan listed among its related medications and report the maximum total dose in milligrams that page allows in 24 hours, and the minimum number of hours to wait before taking a second dose.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open the Migraine condition page /condition/migraine AND the related triptan drug page /drug/sumatriptan. (2) The answer MUST give the maximum total dose in 24 hours (200 mg) AND the minimum wait before a second dose (at least 2 hours). (3) Missing either figure, or an empty answer, is a FAIL.

ques: From the Atrial Fibrillation condition page, open the factor Xa inhibitor anticoagulant listed among its related medications, and report its standard dose for atrial fibrillation plus the three patient criteria the page lists for using the reduced dose.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open /condition/atrial-fibrillation AND the factor Xa inhibitor drug page /drug/apixaban. (2) The answer MUST give the standard AFib dose (5 mg twice daily) AND the three reduced-dose criteria: age 80 or older, body weight 60 kg or less, and elevated creatinine. (3) Missing the dose or any criterion, or an empty answer, is a FAIL.

ques: Open the Gout condition page and report which diuretic its causes section specifically names as a risk factor. Then open the related article about gout attacks that is linked from that page and report who wrote it.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open the Gout condition page /condition/gout AND the linked article /articles/gout-attacks-prevention. (2) The answer MUST name the diuretic risk factor hydrochlorothiazide AND the article's author Curtis Boone. (3) Missing either, or an empty answer, is a FAIL.

ques: Open the condition page for Vertigo (BPPV) and report the name of the repositioning maneuver its treatments section says cures most cases, and the anti-nausea medicine it names for short-term relief.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open the Vertigo (BPPV) condition page /condition/vertigo-bppv. (2) The answer MUST name the repositioning maneuver (Epley maneuver) AND the anti-nausea medicine (ondansetron). (3) Missing either, or an empty answer, is a FAIL.

ques: Use the Symptom Checker: select Dizziness, Heart palpitations, Fatigue, and Shortness of breath, run the check, and report the top-ranked condition and how many of the selected symptoms it matched.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST use the Symptom Checker (/symptom-checker) and reach a results page. (2) The answer MUST report the top-ranked condition (Atrial Fibrillation) AND how many of the 4 selected symptoms it matched (4 of 4). (3) A guessed condition without running the checker, missing the count, or an empty answer is a FAIL.

ques: Use the Symptom Checker: select Fever, Frequent urination, and Painful urination, run the check, and report the top-ranked condition.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST use the Symptom Checker (/symptom-checker) and reach a results page. (2) The answer MUST report the top-ranked condition: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI). (3) A guessed condition without running the checker, or an empty answer, is a FAIL.

ques: Find the author profile of the medical reviewer on this site who is board-certified in Gastroenterology, and report her name and how many articles she has medically reviewed on this site.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open the author profile /authors/lucia-ferreira-md (the reviewer board-certified in Gastroenterology). (2) The answer MUST give her name (Lucia Ferreira, MD) AND how many articles she has medically reviewed on the site (5). (3) Missing the count, wrong reviewer, or an empty answer is a FAIL.

ques: Register a new WebMD account with the name Jordan Rivera, email jordan.rivera@example.com, and password DemoPass789!, then open the account settings page and confirm the name shown on your profile.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST hit /register. (2) A new user account with name 'Jordan Rivera' and email jordan.rivera@example.com MUST exist in the after-state DB and MUST NOT exist in the seed. (3) The answer MUST confirm the profile name Jordan Rivera. Self-reported success with no registered user is a FAIL.

ques: Log in with the demo account (email: alice.j@test.com, password: TestPass123!), open the article about why gout attacks happen at 3 A.M., save it, then go to your saved articles and confirm it now appears in the list.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST hit /login, open /articles/gout-attacks-prevention, and open /account/saved. (2) In the after-state DB, 'gout-attacks-prevention' MUST be in alice.j@test.com's saved list AND MUST NOT have been in her seed saved list. (3) A self-report of saving with no DB change is a FAIL.

ques: Log in with the demo account (email: bob.m@test.com, password: TestPass123!), change the account password to NewPass456! from account settings, log out, and log back in with the new password to confirm the change worked.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open /account (settings) and visit /login at least twice (initial login + re-login after the change). (2) In the after-state DB, bob.m@test.com's stored password hash MUST differ from the seed hash; if bcrypt is available it must verify the new password NewPass456!. (3) A self-report with an unchanged password hash is a FAIL.

ques: Log in with the demo account (email: carol.w@test.com, password: TestPass123!), open your saved articles list, and report how many articles are saved in it.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST hit /login and open /account/saved for carol.w@test.com. (2) The answer MUST report the correct number of saved articles (4, matching the DB). (3) A wrong count or empty answer is a FAIL.

ques: Compare the drug pages for atorvastatin and rosuvastatin: which one's 'Used For' list links more conditions, and which conditions appear on that drug's list but not on the other's?
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: (1) Trajectory MUST open BOTH drug pages /drug/atorvastatin AND /drug/rosuvastatin. (2) The answer MUST state that atorvastatin's 'Used For' list links MORE conditions (4 vs 2) AND identify the two conditions on atorvastatin but not rosuvastatin: Chronic Kidney Disease and Stroke. (3) Wrong winner, missing either unique condition, or an empty answer is a FAIL.
